title: 2.2 omits the totalWithdrawal Executable-window assertion: an off-window broadcast re-initiates the minter-drain (recovers 0), stranding minter principal and wasting an irreversible terminal-migration session
description: The entire 2.2 leg is documented as time-critical and 'must run inside the [init+24h, init+72h] Executable window' (intent.md §4, script header), yet the script never asserts the window. `_executeMinterWithdrawal` blindly calls `oldYS.totalWithdrawal(token, MINTER_V1)`. If the in-flight phase-1 has lapsed (lazy-expiry: status only flips to Expired on the next call), `totalWithdrawal` takes the None/Expired branch in AYieldStrategy and RE-INITIATES a fresh phase-1 instead of executing — recovering 0. `recovered=0` then makes `_seedV2` a no-op (line 164 early return) and, crucially, the minter's principal is NOT drained. The preflight only smoke-reads `principalOf(...) >= 0` (line 207, always true) — it does NOT check the withdrawal status is Executable. Fork-confirmed both windows ARE open at block 25322425 (DOLA initiatedAt=1781371715, USDC=1781371739; block ts 1781520779 within [init+86400, init+259200]), so the happy path works today; but nothing in the script guarantees that on the live broadcast, and the window is the sole timing constraint the runbook is built around. This is a faithfulness deviation: the script does not enforce its own documented time-critical-window intent, so it is also routed to spec-conformance.
impact: No direct theft — InPlaceMigrator invariant C forecloses any path that sends parked principal anywhere but the original user, so High is excluded. Run outside the window: the staker is paused (step1), skimmed (step2), TERMINALLY migrated and drained (step4, no resume path), and rewired (step6) BEFORE the minter-drain at step5. The minter-drain recovers 0, V2 seed is skipped, and `_postAssert`'s `principalOf(token,MINTER_V1)==0` (lines 219-220) fails. Under ordinary simulation forge aborts the whole broadcast atomically (no half-commit); but in a live-divergent run (preview/broadcast divergence across the window edge, or --skip-simulation) the staker has already drained at par into the migrator on the EARLIER successful txs, and the minter ends up with a freshly re-armed 24h phase-1 it must wait out — a wasted, irreversible terminal-migration session, with the minter's ~13816 DOLA + ~11934 USDC left stranded on the retired old strategy. This is the Medium availability/value-leak band (protocol function/availability impacted, value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements); the minimum-guaranteed harm (wasted terminal session + stranded minter principal behind a re-armed 24h window) clears the Medium bar independent of PoC strength on the worse branch.
attackPath: 1. Operator broadcasts 2.2 after the [init+24h, init+72h] Executable window has lapsed (lazy-expiry — status only flips to Expired on the next call).
2. Steps 1-2 pause + skim the live staker; step4 terminally migrates + drains it; step6 rewires.
3. Step5 _executeMinterWithdrawal calls oldYS.totalWithdrawal, which takes the None/Expired branch and re-initiates a fresh phase-1, recovering 0.
4. recovered==0 makes _seedV2 a no-op; minter principal is NOT drained; _postAssert principalOf==0 fails.
5. Under simulation the broadcast aborts atomically (no half-commit); in a live-divergent run the staker has already drained and the minter is left with a re-armed 24h window.
recommendation: Before step5, read `oldYS.withdrawalStates(token, MINTER_V1)` and assert status==Executable AND `block.timestamp <= initiatedAt + TOTAL_DURATION` for BOTH tokens, reverting in preflight (before pause/drain) with the exact `executableAt`/`expiresAt` so the operator aborts cheaply instead of mid-migration. Optionally assert `recovered > 0` right after each `_executeMinterWithdrawal` so a silent re-initiate fails loudly before the rewire rather than at `_postAssert`.
